$comment: WHAT AN ENTRY IS. Not a suppression -- a dated, keyed, reasoned record that a governed job
CANNOT hold its apt budget inside its own timeout, and that this is not being repaired in the
change that discovered it. The job is still printed by --human, still costs exactly what it
costs, and still fails the invariant; what the entry buys is a non-red gate, never a fitting job.
`observedNonAptSeconds` PINS WHAT WAS ACKNOWLEDGED. An entry covers the measurement it names and
nothing worse: if the job's measured non-apt work climbs above this number, the entry stops
covering it and the audit goes red again. A baseline that keeps matching after the thing it
excused has grown is the vacuity class with a filename.
`liftsWhen` NAMES THE GATE THAT WOULD ACTUALLY CLEAR *THIS* ENTRY -- and that phrasing is the
repair of a trap found in this tree on 2026-08-22: a `LIFTS WHEN` STRICTER THAN THE GATE IT
NAMES keeps a deferral alive after its defect is gone. The condition below is exactly the
arithmetic the audit performs on this one job, so satisfying it makes the entry stale.
STALE ENTRIES FAIL. An entry whose job now fits (or which names no governed job at all) is a
claim about CI that stopped being true, and the audit refuses it until it is deleted.

findings.reason: MEASURED 2026-08-22 over the 20 most recent successful runs (see apt-job-timings.measured.json for the run ids): this lane's non-apt work is 571s at p90 and 683s at max, against a 840s cap. With the 420s CI apt budget and the 10s SIGKILL grace that needs 1001s, so the lane is 161s short -- and unlike every other governed job there is no room to find. Its `timeout-minutes: 14` is already one minute under the ubuntu-slim 15-minute runner-class HARD CAP, so raising the timeout is not available. Lowering ZETA_APT_BUDGET_SECONDS for this lane alone would have to reach 840-10-571 = 259s, and its own apt phase has been measured at up to 133s on a slow mirror (run 32546617178), leaving under 2x headroom on the first attempt -- which is the exact trade that the 150s first draft of this budget got wrong on 2026-08-18 (it bounded a stall correctly and false-failed a merely-slow mirror). PR #13476 already took the one cut available on the apt side (tier-gating manifests/apt from 388 packages / 713 MiB to 149 / 139.7 MiB, which moved this lane's apt phase from 148s to 30-66s); what remains over budget is the lane's own dotnet restore + build + test on one vCPU. So this is recorded, with its arithmetic, as a job that cannot be bounded this way today -- not repaired in the change that added the term which found it.
findings.liftsWhen: LIFTS WHEN 420 + 10 + this job's measured nonAptP90Seconds <= 840 -- i.e. when apt-job-timings.measured.json records nonAptP90Seconds <= 410 for this key, reached by cutting the lane's non-apt work (its restore/build/test on 1 vCPU, or its cache-restore steps), or by any change that lowers the budget or raises the cap so the same sum fits. At that point this entry goes STALE, which is itself refused.
